newsitem.title: GREECE: INVESTORS SNAP UP GREEK TELECOM OTE PART-FLOAT.
newsitem.headline: INVESTORS SNAP UP GREEK TELECOM OTE PART-FLOAT.

text.p: Greek telecom OTE's second part-flotation met with a strong welcome in international markets and was oversubscribed three times, said National Bank, global coordinator for the private placement and public offering.
The final price that emerged from the book-building process for institutional investors was 6,600 drachmas per share, near the upper end of the 6,200-6,900 price range announced earlier.
Some 15 months after its 96 billion drachma IPO which preceded its listing on the Athens bourse, OTE tapped international capital markets for an amount close to 350 billion drachmas.

Foreign institutional investors bid for 82 million shares against a total of 45 million initially offered but this was raised by another 8.44 million shares as Greece along with the global coordinators made use of a green-shoe facility.

Domestic institutional investors bid for 17.5 million shares while a record 244,897 retail investors subscribed for a total of about 50 million shares in the Hellenic Telecommunications Organisation -- OTE.
The final price for the public offering to domestic retail investors was set at 6,400 drachmas a share with each applicant allotted a maximum of 80 shares versus the 100-share lot expected earlier.

It was a success for National Bank deputy governor Nick Karamouzis and team, the architects behind the demanding task of global coordination and lead underwriting along with Salomon Brothers and HSBC Investment Banking.
The final allocation of the total 53.4 million flotation had foreign institutionals allotted 48 percent, domestic institutionals 17 percent and retail investors 35 percent.
In Greece, global coordinator National Bank sold one out of every three shares offered, officials said.

As to the geographic breakdown of the foreign institutional tranche, the lion's share -- 45 percent -- came from U.S. based funds while 23 percent came from the U.K. and 32 percent from all other countries.

"International institutional investors, and they numbered over 500, were convinced of OTE's strong prospects. It is certainly a good exposure for Greece and its equities market. We could see a wider interest for further exposure in Greek shares," Karamouzis told Reuters.
For National Bank, itself planning a sizeable rights issue in the coming months, around 100 billion drachmas, the endeavour also meant a significant gain in expertise and know-how.
From a wider perspective, OTE's second successful part-flotation which raised the free float to around 20 percent from 7.6, attracted institutional investors with a longer term investment horizon.
It was a vote of confidence in the telecom's prospects.

OTE which recently signed a deal to acquire 20 percent of New Serbia's PTT -- Telekom Srbije -- and an equal stake in a GSM operator in that country for 675 million marks along with Italian partner Stet , will also launch DCS 1800 mobile telephony with Norway's Telenor.

And this year OTE will beat earlier projections of 304 billion drachmas in pretax earnings and post profit in excess of 320 billion, Greece's Transport and Communications Minister Haris Kastanidis told parliament last week.
On Wednesday, following a long holiday weekend, OTE shares will trade ex-rights as the telecom is headed for a 7.5 percent rights issue at 6,000 drachmas a share which will end July 18.
It will put another 190 billion drachmas in OTE's pockets.

The Greek state will fully exercise its rights. The terms of the rights issue will be six new shares per 80 held. The part-floated shares were stripped of their rights but will get this year's dividend. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
